events.title: Traditional Founding of Rome
events.description: By long-standing Roman tradition, Romulus founded the city of Rome on this day. Romans celebrated the anniversary each year with a festival called the Parilia.
events.significance: Rome grew from a small settlement into a republic and then an empire. Its law, language, engineering and politics still shape the Western world.

events.title: Battle of San Jacinto
events.description: Texian forces under Sam Houston launched a surprise afternoon attack on General Antonio López de Santa Anna's Mexican army. The battle lasted about 18 minutes and ended in a decisive victory.
events.significance: The victory secured Texan independence from Mexico. It paved the way for Texas to join the United States and for the war that followed.

events.title: Mark Twain Dies
events.description: Samuel Clemens, known worldwide as Mark Twain, died at his home in Redding, Connecticut, at age 74. He was the author of The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.
events.significance: Twain helped define a distinctly American literary voice through humor, satire and sharp social observation. Many critics regard Huckleberry Finn as a landmark of American fiction.

events.title: Birth of Queen Elizabeth II
events.description: Princess Elizabeth of York was born in London. She became queen in 1952 and reigned for 70 years.
events.significance: She was the longest-reigning monarch in British history. Her reign spanned the end of empire, the growth of the Commonwealth and enormous social change.

events.title: Brasília Inaugurated
events.description: Brazil officially opened its new capital, Brasília, a planned city built in the interior in just a few years. Architect Oscar Niemeyer and urban planner Lúcio Costa designed it.
events.significance: The city became a bold symbol of modernist design and national ambition. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
